# Genprex Announces New Research Identifying TROP2 as a Potential Predictive Biomarker to Reqorsa® Gene Therapy in Lung Cancer


** November 4, 2026


[Press Releases](https://www.genprex.com/category/press-releases/)[gene therapy](https://www.genprex.com/tag/gene-therapy/)[Lung cancer](https://www.genprex.com/tag/lung-cancer/)[Oncoprex](https://www.genprex.com/tag/oncoprex/)[Reqorsa](https://www.genprex.com/tag/reqorsa/)


*Research to be Presented at the 2026 EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium Links TROP2 Expression to Treatment Response and Explores its Role in Treatment Sensitivity* **


*Findings Suggest Low TROP2 Expression is Associated with Primary Resistance to REQORSA and May Help Guide Patient Selection* **


AUSTIN, Texas — (Nov. 4, 2026) —[Genprex, Inc.](https://www.genprex.com/) (“Genprex” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ:[GNPX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/gnpx) ), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing gene therapies designed to restore tumor-suppressor function in cancer and insulin-producing function in diabetes, today announced new research identifying TROP2 expression as a potential predictive biomarker of response to its lead drug candidate, Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, will be presented at the 2026 EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics, taking place November 18-20, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain.


The research collaborators found that low TROP2 expression was consistently associated with resistance to REQORSA across multiple preclinical models of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This finding was also supported by analysis of pretreatment tumor biopsies from patients enrolled in a clinical trial evaluating REQORSA.


“Discovering an applicable biomarker of response is a meaningful step toward a more precise approach to treating lung cancer with REQORSA,” said Ryan Confer, President and Chief Executive Officer of Genprex. “These data show that low TROP2 expression was associated with primary resistance across multiple preclinical models, and this was supported by analysis of patient biopsies from a clinical trial. If confirmed in further studies, TROP2 could not only help us enhance our clinical trials by recruiting and selecting more applicable patients, but, more importantly, benefit future patients by ultimately delivering potentially more effective, personalized treatment options. This work reflects our commitment to a precision-medicine approach to treating lung cancer.”


The TUSC2 tumor suppressor protein expression is downregulated or absent in more than 80% of NSCLC cases and nearly all small cell lung cancers. Previous studies have shown that REQORSA has antitumor activity, including in models resistant to targeted therapies and in immunotherapy-resistant KRAS/LKB1-mutant NSCLC. REQORSA’s effects are mediated by inhibiting MAPK and mTOR signaling, inducing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis, and activating antitumor immune responses.


Key findings from the research include:


- **TROP2 expression associated with resistance** : Approximately 50% of 10 NSCLC cell lines and 50% of 12 patient derived organoid models evaluated showed primary resistance to TUSC2 gene delivery. Protein-expression analyses consistently identified low TROP2 expression as a marker associated with resistance across multiple preclinical models.
- **Supporting clinical evidence:** Analysis of pretreatment tumor biopsies from patients enrolled in a TUSC2 gene therapy clinical trial supported the association between TROP2 expression and treatment response.
- **TROP2 modulation influenced treatment sensitivity:** Experimental manipulation of TROP2 expression altered TUSC2-induced cancer cell death, suggesting that TROP2-dependent signaling may play a role in therapeutic response. Further research is underway to understand these context-dependent effects.


Collectively, the findings identify TROP2 as a potential predictive biomarker for response to REQORSA and suggest that modulating TROP2 signaling may be a novel strategy to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of REQORSA in NSCLC. While these findings provide preclinical and supportive clinical evidence, additional research and prospective clinical evaluation will be required to establish TROP2’s predictive utility in patients receiving REQORSA.


**The featured Genprex-supported poster is to be presented at the 2026 EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics:**


**Title:** TROP2 Predicts Response to TUSC2 Gene Therapy (Quaratusugene Ozeplasmid) and Its Modulation Sensitizes Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer to Treatment


**Conference:** 2026 EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics


**Topic:** Drug Resistance and Modifiers ****

**About Reqorsa® Gene Therapy**


Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, consists of a plasmid containing the TUSC2 gene encapsulated in non-viral lipid-based nanoparticles in a lipoplex form (the Company’s Oncoprex® Delivery System), which has a positive charge. REQORSA is injected intravenously and specifically targets cancer cells. REQORSA is designed to deliver the functioning TUSC2 gene to negatively charged cancer cells while minimizing uptake by normal tissue. Laboratory studies conducted at MD Anderson show that the uptake of TUSC2 in tumor cells in vitro after REQORSA treatment was 10 to 33 times the uptake in normal cells.


**About Genprex, Inc.**


Genprex, Inc. is a clinical-stage gene therapy company focusing on developing innovative treatments designed to restore biological functions disrupted by disease. The Company’s lead oncology program, Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, is being developed for the treatment of lung cancer and is designed to deliver the TUSC2 tumor suppressor gene to help restore tumor-suppressive activity and address multiple pathways involved in cancer progression.


The Company’s lead candidate, REQORSA, uses the systemic, non-viral ONCOPREX® Delivery System to deliver the TUSC2 tumor suppressor gene via a non-viral lipid-based nanoparticle. REQORSA is designed to restore tumor-suppressor function and is being evaluated in the Acclaim-1 and Acclaim-3 clinical trials for non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer, respectively. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track Designation to both lung cancer programs and Orphan Drug designation to the small cell lung cancer program.


Genprex is also advancing an earlier stage gene therapy program for diabetes, designed to restore insulin-producing capability through the expression of key pancreatic transcription factors. Across its programs, Genprex is focused on translating innovative gene therapy approaches into meaningful therapeutic advances for patients with significant unmet medical needs.
